result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unmarked asphalt roadway passing under a large bridge structure. While sidewalks are present, the lack of marked crosswalks and pedestrian signals at a signalized intersection creates significant exposure for people crossing the street.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalk markings at this signalized intersection, leaving pedestrians without a designated path.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground where the brick sidewalk meets the asphalt roadway.

hazards.name: Poor Visibility Under Bridge
hazards.description: The large overpass creates deep shadows that can obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: The roadway area directly beneath the green bridge structure.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, forcing pedestrians to interpret vehicle signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.
hazards.location_in_image: On the traffic light pole in the center of the image.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style high-visibility crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve crossing safety and predictability.

interventions.title: Under-Bridge Lighting
interventions.description: Add supplemental lighting beneath the overpass to eliminate dark spots and improve visibility of pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is significantly impacted by active construction, with fencing and orange barriers obstructing walkways and sightlines. While sidewalks and traffic signals are present, the lack of marked crosswalks and clear pedestrian routing through the intersection creates a hazardous environment.

hazards.name: Construction Obstructions
hazards.description: Chain-link fencing and orange plastic barriers block the sidewalk and force pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, extending into the foreground

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crosswalks
hazards.description: No painted crosswalks are visible at this signalized intersection, increasing pedestrian exposure.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground asphalt area

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: Cracked and uneven asphalt surfaces near the construction zone create trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and right side near barriers

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Access Route
interventions.description: Establish a clearly marked and protected walkway through the construction zone to maintain pedestrian connectivity.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian space at the intersection.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Install pedestrian countdown signals to provide clear crossing intervals for people on foot.

result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection undergoing major construction, with the roadway completely excavated and fenced off. Pedestrians are confined to a narrow brick sidewalk that is partially obstructed by construction signage and temporary barriers.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Construction signs and fencing significantly narrow the usable pedestrian walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground and midground on the brick sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of Crossing Infrastructure
hazards.description: The roadway is completely removed, and no clear temporary crossing or detour is visible for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and left foreground where the road should be

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Construction equipment and fencing block sightlines between pedestrians and any potential traffic beyond the site.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and center background

interventions.title: Temporary Pedestrian Access Route (TPAR)
interventions.description: Establish a clearly marked, ADA-compliant temporary path that maintains a consistent width and provides a smooth surface.

interventions.title: Signage Relocation
interventions.description: Move construction signage out of the primary pedestrian clear zone to prevent bottlenecks.

interventions.title: Temporary Wayfinding
interventions.description: Install clear detour signage to guide pedestrians safely around the construction zone to the nearest accessible crossing.

result.summary: The environment features wide, well-maintained sidewalks and a substantial bus shelter, but lacks marked pedestrian crossings or traffic control devices at the immediate intersection. The presence of a transit stop without visible crossing infrastructure creates a disconnect between pedestrian needs and road design.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: No marked crosswalk is visible near a major bus stop, forcing pedestrians to cross without designated space.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground intersection area

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or signals are visible to manage vehicle-pedestrian interactions at this junction.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install continental-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Signage
interventions.description: Add 'Yield to Pedestrian' signs to alert drivers of the crossing location.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the crossing point to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility.
